openings.claim: Use the first parent function alone: materialize common-unit comparison values in V alongside every original quantity, unit and record citation. This changes the comparison carrier from repeated conversions to inspectable columns; it does not establish which revision is authoritative.
openings.delta: For each recorded quantity apply only U=5V, retaining originals. Preserve every duplicate and unmatched row individually. For all twelve batches report a cited reconciled quantity only when normalized records support it unambiguously; otherwise report explicit bounded disagreement. Do not infer missing quantities from neighbors or link replacements as a second-parent operation. List amendment and status ambiguities as unresolved evidence. Issue at most three requests, each naming a missing field or record; retain other unresolved gaps visibly.
openings.prediction: Against the ordinary rival of pairwise spreadsheet comparisons with the same supplied conversion factor and identical conservative reporting rules, stored normalized columns may reduce conversion mistakes or time spent reconverting duplicates. Both should recognize the stipulated seven conversion agreements; that observation alone cannot distinguish them. Distinguishing observations are variant differences in key-correct resolved-batch counts, unsupported definite claims, elapsed time and request counts. No improvement is established.
openings.probe: Bounded workflow probe, not deployment: run each variant on each supplied copy, allocating fifteen minutes per run, sixty reviewer minutes total. Freeze twelve batch outcomes with citations and a complete row ledger per run; use the supplied extra twenty minutes to open the sealed key and compare scores. On the disturbed copy, the missing superseded-row reference and undefined status must remain explicit ambiguities without invented quantities or meanings. Record incomplete ledgers as failed completion, not successful disagreement outputs. Stop limits alone do not prove informative feasibility.
assumptions: The stipulated records, conversion table, spreadsheet or script, two copies and sealed key are available; their contents beyond supplied observations are unknown.
Capacity to inspect all rows and produce traceable outcomes within the allocated probe time is unproven. Any missed completion defeats feasibility under this probe.

No conversion-error advantage, worse key correctness, or new unsupported definite claims defeats the proposed benefit. Revision ambiguity, undefined statuses and limited requests can leave disagreement; normalization cannot cure them.

assessment: One first-parent-only opening. Constraint-preserving intent with unmeasured benefit and unproven timing. Cross-row amendment equivalence remains unresolved rather than becoming a coupling with the revision-register parent.
